messages:
Priya (CSE): Hi team — Acme (enterprise) opened an escalation. After today's sampling update they report a noticeable style/length change in answers (more hedging, less step-by-step). They included two before/after snips.

Acme Support: "Before (v1.3): 'Sure — here's a 4-step migration plan with commands and pitfalls.'
After (v1.4+spec): 'I might not be able to help with that right now.'" Request ID: req_8abc123. This started right after the 08:13UTC canary. P1 for them, CI acceptance tests failing.

Marco (ML Eng): Can you confirm model + rollout id + exact payload? Any temperature/beam changes? Speculative sampler can shift distribution if draft scoring/regret isn't tuned.

Acme Support: Model: redwood-open-1.4 (server reports rev 2026-03-17-14f). Rollout: r/2026-03-17/spec-draft-v2. Payload included decode.policy=speculative with draft_tokens=6. No other notable header changes.

Noah (Runtime Eng): We rolled the canary to 10% at 08:13 UTC, rollout id matches. Config: draft_tokens=6, draft_ratio=0.6, final_scoring=enabled. CPU/GPU telemetry looked normal; small tail latency improvement. Possible side-effect: draft scoring can favor shorter safe completions in some prompts.

Priya (CSE): Repro steps Acme sent (they ran locally against our hosted endpoint):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 -d '{
  "model": "redwood-open-1.4",
  "input": "How do I migrate DB schema without downtime?",
  "decode": {"policy": "speculative", "draft_tokens": 6}
}'
```
They get the short/hedging answer. With decode.policy=greedy they get the long step-by-step baseline.

Sophie (Product): Severity P1 confirmed by CSM. This blocks their rollout. Do we have a hotfix path (org-level override) while we investigate?

Noah (Runtime Eng): Yes — we can pin org-level decode overrides. I'll apply a temporary per-tenant override for acme-corp to set decode.policy=greedy and draft_tokens=0.

Jules (SRE): Adding logs to capture per-request decode policy, model rev, and response token counts so we can surface token-delta regressions per tenant.

Noah (Runtime Eng): Executing now: `rbctl org update acme-corp --set decode.policy=greedy --set decode.draft_tokens=0`

ops-bot: rollout r/2026-03-17/spec-draft-v2 scaled to 0% at 08:37 UTC (triggered by manual rollback).

Priya (CSE): Confirmed with Acme — after the override they see baseline outputs and their acceptance tests pass again. They've accepted the mitigation for now. Logged ticket CH-4572 and scheduled a follow-up next week.

Marco (ML Eng): Next steps from ML side: run an offline A/B over the curated Acme eval set + our regression suite to quantify accuracy/verbosity deltas across draft_tokens in {0,4,6,8} and draft_ratio sweep. Also investigate final_scoring weighting to reduce short-answer bias.

Jules (SRE): We'll add an automated alert: if tenant average response length changes by >25% vs baseline within 2 hours of a rollout, page the oncall. Also persisting tenant decode config in trace logs for audits.

Sophie (Product): Thanks. Can we add a checklist to the rollout runbook: include regression evals against top-5 customers' test prompts before enabling speculative globally?

Marco (ML Eng): Agreed — I'll open a PR to the rollout playbook with the eval gating.

Priya (CSE): Great work — Acme is unblocked. Leaving action items: CH-4572 (follow-up A/B + tuning), RB-7890 (runbook change), infra ticket to persist decode config in logs. Thanks everyone :heart:

Acme Support: Thanks so much — confirm we'll reach out if anything else crops up.
